items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Pedro Reyes, a Mexican artist, often responds to gun violence in his sculptures and public projects.
• For Palas por Pistolas (2008), Reyes collected 1,527 weapons that residents of Culiacán, Mexico, donated in exchange for coupons.
• The weapons were melted down and forged into 1,527 shovels for planting trees.
• For Imagine (2012), he received 6,700 weapons confiscated by authorities in Ciudad Juárez.
• Working with six musicians, he turned the weapons’ metal parts into fifty playable instruments.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Palas por Pistolas and Imagine. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the weapons in Palas por Pistolas became shovels, those in Imagine became musical instruments.
Palas por Pistolas and Imagine are both made from weapons that Reyes obtained in Mexico.
For Imagine, Reyes received 6,700 weapons that authorities in Ciudad Juárez had confiscated.
Pedro Reyes is a Mexican artist whose sculptures and public projects often respond to gun violence.
items.explanation: The goal asks for something the two works have in common. The notes say that Palas por Pistolas was made from weapons donated in Culiacán and that Imagine was made from weapons confiscated in Ciudad Juárez, so both works are made from weapons Reyes obtained in Mexico, as choice B says.

A.recipe: REL: wrong relation or wrong dimension
A.why_wrong: It sets the two works against each other with “whereas,” pointing out what each became, which is a difference, not a similarity.

C.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
C.why_wrong: It describes where the weapons for Imagine came from but never mentions Palas por Pistolas, so nothing is compared.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
D.why_wrong: It introduces the artist and his usual subject but names neither work, so it shows no similarity between them.

sources.what: Palas por Pistolas: commissioned by Culiacán; TV ads offered coupons redeemable at local stores in exchange for guns; 1,527 weapons collected, crushed by a steamroller, melted and forged into 1,527 shovelheads used to plant trees

Imagine (2012): 6,700 confiscated weapons from Ciudad Juárez offered by a government official; six musicians over two weeks; 50 wind, percussion and string instruments; Palas por Pistolas 2008, 1,527 weapons into 1,527 shovels
Mexican artist Pedro Reyes; Palas por pistolas 2008 (weapons donated by civilians in Culiacán) and Imagine 2012 (metal from a weapons decommissioning program), works responding to gun violence

items.notes: Some sources give 7,000 weapons for Imagine; 6,700 is the figure in most reports.
items.rewrite: New subject (Pedro Reyes, Palas por Pistolas and Imagine) replacing the famous Arecibo and FAST telescopes; no duplicated bullet sets up the shared trait, which now has to be drawn from two differently worded pairs of notes.

items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Japanese lacquerware is often decorated with maki-e, raden, or both.
• In maki-e, a design drawn in wet lacquer is sprinkled with metal powder, usually gold or silver.
• The term maki-e means “sprinkled picture.”
• In raden, iridescent pieces of shell are cut into shapes and embedded in the lacquered surface.
• This technique came to Japan from Tang dynasty China.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between maki-e and raden. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Maki-e and raden are two different techniques that artisans use to decorate Japanese lacquerware.
Raden, a technique that came to Japan from Tang dynasty China, uses iridescent pieces of shell.
Maki-e decorates lacquer with sprinkled metal powder, while raden uses pieces of shell.
Maki-e, a term that means “sprinkled picture,” is one technique used to decorate Japanese lacquerware.
items.explanation: To emphasize a difference, the sentence must set the two techniques side by side on the same point. Choice C does this for the material each one adds to the lacquer: maki-e uses sprinkled metal powder, while raden uses pieces of shell.

A.recipe: VAGUE: names the relation without the content
A.why_wrong: It says the techniques are different but never says how, so no actual difference is emphasized.

B.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
B.why_wrong: It describes raden only and never mentions maki-e, so nothing is contrasted.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
D.why_wrong: It gives the meaning of the term maki-e and its use on lacquerware but says nothing about raden, so no difference is shown.

sources.what: Maki-e: “sprinkled picture”; design drawn in lacquer, metal powder (gold, silver, other metals) sprinkled onto the wet lacquer; often combined with raden, in which mother-of-pearl nacre is embedded in or pasted onto lacquer
Raden: inlay of nacre (shell) into lacquer; the technique (Chinese luodian) was introduced from the Tang dynasty into Japan during the Nara period
Raden: shell pieces cut into designs with a knife or needle and glued onto the lacquered surface (usugai method); flourished in the Nara period
Japan Tourism Agency multilingual database: raden embeds small pieces of mother of pearl in lacquer; introduced from China in the eighth century (Shōsōin relics); maki-e often used with raden

fixes: key joined with “while” instead of “whereas” (the file overused “whereas”, 7 items against the bank’s 10 of 92)

items.rewrite: New subject (maki-e and raden lacquer decoration) replacing the textbook shield volcano and stratovolcano contrast; the two techniques are no longer described in mirror-image bullets.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Italian printer Juan Pablos began printing in Mexico City in 1539.
• Antonio Ricardo, a printer from Turin, Italy, set up the first press in Lima, Peru, in 1584.
• Ricardo’s catechism in Spanish, Quechua, and Aymara is considered the first book printed in South America.
• Stephen Daye began operating a press in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1639.
items.stem: The student wants to identify which of the three cities was the first to have a printing press. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Printing began in Mexico City in 1539, decades before presses were operating in Lima (1584) and Cambridge (1639).
Antonio Ricardo established Lima’s first press in 1584, decades before Daye began printing in Cambridge.
A catechism printed by Antonio Ricardo in Lima is considered the first book printed in South America.
Printers from Italy began printing in both Mexico City and Lima during the sixteenth century.
items.explanation: The goal asks which of the three cities had a printing press first. The notes date the first press in Mexico City to 1539, in Lima to 1584 and in Cambridge to 1639, so choice A correctly names Mexico City and shows that it came before both of the others.

B.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
B.why_wrong: It compares only Lima and Cambridge and leaves out Mexico City, the city that had a press first.

C.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
C.why_wrong: It says Lima produced the first book printed in South America, a different first that does not show which of the three cities had a press earliest.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
D.why_wrong: It points out that both early printers came from Italy, which is about who the printers were, not which city had a press first.

sources.what: Juan Pablos (Giovanni Paoli), Italian printer from Lombardy sent to Mexico City by Juan Cromberger of Seville; printing in Mexico City began 1539; first documented printer in the Americas

Antonio Ricardo, Italian from Turin, first printer in South America, worked in Lima from 1584; Doctrina christiana (1584), trilingual in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara, generally cited as the first book printed in South America
Antonio Ricardo, a 16th-century printer in Mexico City and Lima; Lima press from 1584
Stephen Daye ran the first printing press in British North America at Cambridge, Massachusetts, from 1639

items.notes: Some sources date Daye’s first Cambridge printing to 1638/1639; 1639 is the usual date for the start of operation.
items.rewrite: Replaced the three moons and their numeric orbit data (an uncertain tell) with the first printing presses in Mexico City, Lima and Cambridge; key keeps the dates in parentheses and the trap options are a two-city comparison, a different first and a shared trait.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Shubayqa 1 is an archaeological site in Jordan’s Black Desert.
• Natufian hunter-gatherers lived there about 14,600 to 11,600 years ago.
• Two of its buildings each had a stone fireplace.
• In 2018, Amaia Arranz-Otaegui’s team reported charred bits of flatbread in the fireplaces.
• The bread was made from wild einkorn, a relative of wheat, and tubers of club-rush, a sedge.
items.stem: The student wants to specify what the bread found at Shubayqa 1 was made from. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Shubayqa 1, a site in Jordan’s Black Desert, was home to Natufian hunter-gatherers about 14,600 to 11,600 years ago.
Two buildings at Shubayqa 1, an archaeological site in Jordan, each had a stone fireplace.
Arranz-Otaegui’s team found charred bits of flatbread in the fireplaces at Shubayqa 1.
According to the 2018 study, the flatbread from Shubayqa 1 was made from wild einkorn and club-rush tubers.
items.explanation: The goal asks what the bread was made from. The last note gives the ingredients, wild einkorn and club-rush tubers, and choice D states them for the flatbread from Shubayqa 1.

A.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
A.why_wrong: It says where the site is and when people lived there, which does not tell what the bread was made from.

B.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
B.why_wrong: It describes the fireplaces in which the bread was found, not the bread’s ingredients.

C.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
C.why_wrong: It reports that flatbread was found but never says what it was made from.

sources.what: Arranz-Otaegui et al. 2018, PNAS: 24 charred food remains from Shubayqa 1, a Natufian hunter-gatherer site in northeastern Jordan dated to 14.6–11.6 ka cal BP; flat bread-like products made from wild einkorn (Triticum boeoticum) and club-rush tubers (Bolboschoenus glaucus)

University of Copenhagen release: archaeobotanist Amaia Arranz Otaegui, first author; flatbread baked 14,400 years ago; site in the Black Desert, northeastern Jordan; two buildings, each with a stone fireplace; predates agriculture by at least 4,000 years
PNAS abstract via Crossref: wild ancestors of domesticated cereals (e.g. wild einkorn) and club-rush tubers used to produce flat bread-like products
Bolboschoenus (club-rush) is a genus in the sedge family, Cyperaceae
Einkorn wheat: wild einkorn (Triticum boeoticum) is the wild form of einkorn, a species of wheat

items.rewrite: New subject (Arranz-Otaegui 2018, Natufian flatbread at Shubayqa 1) replacing the ultra-famous Rosetta Stone; the goal now asks for the bread’s ingredients rather than a find spot.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Madagascar is home to a group of miniaturized leaf chameleons in the genus Brookesia.
• In 2021, Frank Glaw’s team described a new species in this group, Brookesia nana.
• They had just two specimens, both collected in northern Madagascar.
• The male’s body is only 13.5 millimeters long, not counting the tail.
• The team suggests that B. nana may be the world’s smallest reptile.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize how small Brookesia nana is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: With a body only 13.5 millimeters long, the male Brookesia nana may be the smallest reptile in the world.
Brookesia nana belongs to a group of leaf chameleons found in Madagascar.
Glaw’s team described Brookesia nana in 2021 on the basis of just two specimens.
The two specimens of Brookesia nana that Glaw’s team described were both collected in northern Madagascar.
items.explanation: To emphasize the species’ size, the sentence must foreground how small it is. Choice A gives the male’s body length of only 13.5 millimeters and adds that the species may be the world’s smallest reptile.

B.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
B.why_wrong: It classifies the species as one of Madagascar’s leaf chameleons but says nothing about how small it is.

C.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
C.why_wrong: It stresses how few specimens the team had, not how small the animal is.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
D.why_wrong: It tells where the specimens were collected, which says nothing about how small the animal is.

sources.what: Glaw et al. 2021, Scientific Reports 11: 2522: new miniaturized chameleon described from two individuals; male holotype snout–vent length 13.5 mm (total 21.6 mm); may be the world’s smallest reptile species; known only from a degraded montane rainforest in northern Madagascar; part of the clade of miniaturized Brookesia species
Brookesia nana: described in 2021 by Frank Glaw et al.; Sorata massif, northern Madagascar; one male and one female known
Male just shy of 14 mm snout to cloaca, female 19 mm; possibly the smallest reptile on Earth; Brookesia are leaf chameleons

items.notes: “Body ... not counting the tail” renders the paper’s snout–vent length.
items.rewrite: New subject (Glaw 2021, Brookesia nana) replacing the godwit nonstop-flight news record; the size claim keeps the paper’s hedge and the distractors are plain off-goal facts rather than polished paraphrases.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Teresita Fernández is a Cuban American artist known for her public sculptures.
• In 2015, she installed Fata Morgana in Madison Square Park in New York City.
• The work ran for about 500 feet above the park’s walkways.
• It was made of golden, mirror-polished metal discs that formed canopies over the paths.
• The discs were cut with patterns that resembled foliage.
items.stem: The student wants to describe the discs used in Fata Morgana. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Fata Morgana is an installation by Teresita Fernández, a Cuban American artist known for her public sculptures.
Fata Morgana’s golden, mirror-polished discs were cut with patterns that resembled foliage.
Fata Morgana was installed in 2015 in Madison Square Park in New York City.
Fata Morgana ran for about 500 feet above the walkways of Madison Square Park.
items.explanation: To describe the discs, the sentence must say what they looked like. Choice B merges the last two notes: the discs were golden and mirror-polished and were cut with patterns that resembled foliage.

A.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
A.why_wrong: It identifies the artist behind the work but says nothing about what its discs looked like.

C.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
C.why_wrong: It gives the year and place of the installation, not a description of its discs.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
D.why_wrong: It tells how far the work extended and where, but not what its discs looked like.

sources.what: Teresita Fernández: born 1968 in Miami to Cuban exile parents; New York-based visual artist known for public sculptures and unconventional use of materials; Fata Morgana opened June 1, 2015, in Madison Square Park, 500 running feet of gold, mirror-polished discs forming canopies over the paths around the central lawn

Fata Morgana (June 1, 2015 to January 10, 2016): about 500 running feet of golden, mirror-polished metal discs forming canopies over the walkways around the park’s central Oval Lawn; metal pierced with patterns resembling foliage
Madison Square Park Conservancy description: golden, mirror-polished discs creating canopies above the pathways; perforated patterns suggesting foliage

items.notes: “Cuban American” rests on her birth in Miami to Cuban exile parents.
items.rewrite: New subject (Teresita Fernández, Fata Morgana) replacing the famous Guggenheim building; the goal now targets one physical feature of a lesser-known public work.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Okavango Delta, an inland wetland in northern Botswana, does not drain into any sea or ocean.
• Its floodwater originates as rainfall in Angola’s central highlands, where the rainy season lasts from about September to April.
• The Okavango River transports this water slowly southward, so it reaches the delta months later.
• The delta’s inundated area is largest from July to September, late in Botswana’s dry season.
items.stem: The student wants to explain why the Okavango Delta floods during Botswana’s dry season. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Okavango Delta is an inland wetland in northern Botswana that does not drain into any sea or ocean.
The Okavango Delta’s inundated area is largest from July to September, late in Botswana’s dry season.
Rainfall from Angola’s central highlands is transported slowly southward by the Okavango River.
Because its floodwater falls as rain in Angola months earlier, the Okavango Delta floods during Botswana’s dry season.
items.explanation: An explanation must link the flood to its cause. The notes say the floodwater falls as rain in the Angolan highlands and travels slowly south, reaching the delta months later, so the flood peaks late in Botswana’s dry season. Choice D makes that link with “because.”

A.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
A.why_wrong: It describes what kind of place the delta is and notes that it does not drain into a sea, which says nothing about when or why it floods.

B.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
B.why_wrong: It states when the delta’s inundated area is largest but gives no reason, so nothing is explained.

C.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
C.why_wrong: It describes where the floodwater comes from and how it travels but never says that the delta floods in the dry season, so the cause is not tied to the flooding.

sources.what: Okavango Delta: interior delta in the endorheic Kalahari basin of Botswana that does not flow into a sea or ocean; river carries summer rainfall from the Angola highlands; flood levels peak between June and August, during Botswana’s dry winter months
Summer rains between November and March in the Angolan highlands; the water makes a slow, roughly four-month journey south into the delta; peak flood in the middle of Botswana’s dry winter

Lourenco et al. (2023), Environmental Monitoring and Assessment: Angolan Highlands rainfall season from September to April, dry season May to August; the annual Okavango Delta flood occurs out of phase with the rainfall season, inundated area lowest in January–February and highest in July–September during the late dry season

items.notes: Flood timing and the Angolan rainy season follow Lourenco et al. 2023 (peer reviewed); the earlier “November to March” and “four months” figures came from a tourism site and sources disagree on the travel time, so the notes now say “months.”

fixes: replaced tourism-site figures (rain November to March, a four-month journey, peak June to August) with the peer-reviewed timing in Lourenco et al. 2023 (rain September to April, flooded area largest July to September); options B and C reworded to match

items.rewrite: New subject (the Okavango Delta’s dry-season flood) replacing the textbook helium-from-helios anecdote; the key now has to join the timing of the Angolan rains and the slow journey to the flood.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A ghost forest is a stand of dead trees killed by saltwater intrusion, the movement of seawater inland.
• Rising sea levels and storm surges can drive seawater into low-lying coastal forests.
• A 2021 study led by Emily Ury used satellite imagery to map vegetation changes in North Carolina’s Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge.
• Between 1985 and 2019, as much as 11% of the refuge’s forested area became ghost forest.
items.stem: The student wants to define the term “ghost forest” and provide an example of one. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish these goals?
options: One example of a ghost forest can be found in North Carolina’s Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge.
Using satellite imagery, Ury’s team mapped vegetation changes from 1985 to 2019 in a wildlife refuge in coastal North Carolina.
A ghost forest, a stand of dead trees killed by saltwater intrusion, can be found in North Carolina’s Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge.
Rising sea levels and storm surges can drive seawater into low-lying coastal forests, killing the trees.
items.explanation: The goals require both a definition and an example. Choice C defines a ghost forest as a stand of dead trees killed by saltwater intrusion and names an example: the notes say ghost forest has spread across part of North Carolina’s Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge.

A.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
A.why_wrong: It gives an example but never explains what a ghost forest is, so the term is not defined.

B.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
B.why_wrong: It describes the study’s method and setting but neither defines the term nor names a ghost forest.

D.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
D.why_wrong: It explains how seawater can kill coastal trees, close to a definition, but never uses the term or gives an example.

sources.what: Duke release: ghost forests are relics of forests overrun by the inland creep of seawater; rising seas and higher storm surges push saltwater inland; Ury, Yang, Wright and Bernhardt, Ecological Applications, April 4, 2021; 35 years of Landsat images of a 245,000-acre area including Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge; between 1985 and 2019, 11% of the area’s tree cover was taken over by ghost forests

Ury et al. 2021 abstract: rising water tables and salinization penetrate inland, with dramatic changes in freshwater forested wetlands in areas of low topographic relief and low elevation; ghost forest, a land cover type characterized by standing dead trees and fallen trunks; as much as 11% of forested cover in the refuge transitioned to ghost forest; first attempt to map coastal ghost forests using remote sensing

fixes: the notes said only that the study area “includes” the refuge, so the key’s claim that a ghost forest is found in the refuge was an inference; the notes now follow the paper’s abstract (as much as 11% of the refuge’s forest cover became ghost forest, 1985 to 2019); option B and the attribution (“a study led by”) reworded

items.rewrite: New subject (Ury 2021, ghost forests in North Carolina) replacing the textbook microfinance example; the key has to join the definition and the named example, and one distractor is a near-definition without the term.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Chuño is a freeze-dried potato traditionally produced by Quechua and Aymara communities in the Andes.
• Bitter, frost-resistant potatoes are spread on the ground and left outdoors for several nights.
• Exposed to freezing night temperatures and daytime sun, the potatoes freeze and then dehydrate.
• Producers then trample them by foot to expel water and remove the skins.
• Once dried, chuño can be stored for years.
items.stem: The student wants to provide an overview of how chuño is made. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: To produce chuño, potatoes are left outdoors to freeze at night and dehydrate by day and are then trampled to expel water.
Chuño is produced from bitter, frost-resistant potatoes that are spread on the ground and left outdoors for several nights.
Produced by Quechua and Aymara communities in the Andes, chuño can be stored for years once dried.
Trampling potatoes by foot is a way to expel their water and remove their skins.
items.explanation: An overview of the process has to touch each of its stages. Choice A covers them in order: the potatoes are left outdoors, freeze at night and dehydrate by day, and are then trampled to expel water.

B.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
B.why_wrong: It gives only the first stage, the kind of potato and how it is left outdoors, and leaves out the freezing, drying and trampling.

C.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
C.why_wrong: It says who produces chuño and how long it keeps, not how it is made.

D.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
D.why_wrong: It describes a single step, the trampling, without the freezing and drying that come before it.

sources.what: Chuño: preserved potato (natural freeze-drying) traditionally made by Quechua and Aymara communities of Bolivia and Peru; bitter, frost-resistant potatoes exposed to low night temperatures, freezing at night and dehydrating in the daytime for about three nights; then trampled by foot to remove water and skins; can last decades once dried
Black chuño: bitter potatoes left to freeze overnight then crushed to remove the liquids inside until dehydrated

Peer-reviewed survey of Aymara food processing (Frontiers in Nutrition 2026): chuño made by arranging potatoes on the ground under night frost and daytime sun; black chuño relies on frost exposure, trampling and sun-drying and can be stored for years
Bitter Andean potatoes are used to prepare freeze-dried, dehydrated chuño, which is highly storable (Polymers 2023)

fixes: “about three nights” (Wikipedia only; peer-reviewed accounts give three to six freeze-thaw cycles) generalised to “several nights”; “stored for decades” corrected to “for years” (black chuño, per a peer-reviewed survey; multi-decade storage is reported for white tunta); options B and C updated

items.rewrite: New subject (Andean chuño) replacing the textbook Bessemer process; notes follow the process stage by stage and each distractor gives one stage or an off-goal fact.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Pacita Abad (1946–2004) was a Filipino American painter.
• Her best-known works are trapunto paintings, named after a quilting technique.
• To make them, she stitched and stuffed her painted canvases to give them a sculptural effect.
• She often attached materials such as cloth, mirrors, beads, and shells to their surfaces.
• Her final project was painting Singapore’s Alkaff Bridge with 2,350 multicolored circles.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce Pacita Abad to an audience unfamiliar with the artist. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Abad’s trapunto paintings often have cloth, mirrors, beads, and shells attached to their stitched and stuffed canvases.
In her final project, Pacita Abad (1946–2004) painted Singapore’s Alkaff Bridge with 2,350 multicolored circles.
The trapunto paintings that Abad is known for take their name from a quilting technique.
Filipino American painter Pacita Abad’s best-known works are her trapunto paintings, canvases she stitched and stuffed for a sculptural effect.
items.explanation: An audience unfamiliar with Abad first needs to know who she is. Choice D identifies her as a Filipino American painter and then names her best-known works, her stitched and stuffed trapunto paintings.

A.recipe: AUD: audience mismatch (no identifying context)
A.why_wrong: It describes the paintings in detail but refers to “Abad” without ever saying who she is.

B.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
B.why_wrong: It reports her last project, painting a bridge, but does not tell an unfamiliar reader who she was or what she is known for.

C.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
C.why_wrong: It explains where the name of her paintings comes from, which assumes the reader already knows the artist.

sources.what: Pacita Abad: Filipino-American visual artist and painter, born October 1946 in Basco, Batanes, died December 7, 2004; trapunto paintings integrate stitched and stuffed fabric with painting to produce a sculptural effect; added cloth, mirrors, beads, shells and buttons; painted the 55-meter Alkaff Bridge in Singapore with 2,350 circles in the months before her death
Trapunto painting named after a quilting technique: stitching and stuffing painted canvases for a three-dimensional, sculptural effect; Alkaff Bridge (2003–2004), her final project
Pacita Abad biography: trapunto paintings, Alkaff Bridge as a gift to Singapore

items.rewrite: New subject (Pacita Abad) replacing Tarsila do Amaral’s famous painting; the distractors are details of her work that never say who she is, and the key leads with the identifying phrase.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Yi qi, a small dinosaur described in 2015, lived about 159 million years ago in present-day Hebei, China.
• Its wings were formed by skin stretched between its fingers and a long, rod-like wrist bone.
• Ambopteryx longibrachium, described in 2019, lived about 163 million years ago in Liaoning, China.
• Remnants of a wing membrane are preserved alongside its rod-like wrist bones.
• Its stomach held gizzard stones and bone fragments.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Yi qi and Ambopteryx. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Yi qi lived about 159 million years ago, whereas Ambopteryx lived some four million years earlier.
The wings of Yi qi were formed by skin stretched between its fingers and a long wrist bone.
Yi qi and Ambopteryx both had rod-like wrist bones and wings made of a skin membrane.
Ambopteryx, whose stomach held gizzard stones and bone fragments, was described in 2019.
items.explanation: The notes describe each dinosaur’s wings separately: Yi qi’s were skin stretched to a rod-like wrist bone, and Ambopteryx preserves a wing membrane beside rod-like wrist bones. Choice C draws out what the two share, using “both.”

A.recipe: REL: wrong relation or wrong dimension
A.why_wrong: It contrasts when the two dinosaurs lived, which is a difference, not a similarity.

B.recipe: PART: delivers only part of what the goal needs
B.why_wrong: It describes only Yi qi’s wings and never mentions Ambopteryx, so nothing is compared.

D.recipe: OG: accurate, but serves another goal
